— Bicycle Laws and Safety","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Bicycle Laws and Safety

FACT_ID: sec13-F01 | anchor: A01
Texas treats a bicycle as a vehicle, so a rider holds the same rights and owes the same duties as any vehicle driver except where a rule cannot by its nature fit a bicycle [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F02 | anchor: A01
Breaking a traffic law on a bicycle draws the same penalty as breaking it in a motor vehicle, and every traffic conviction goes on the rider's driver record no matter which one they were operating [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F03 | anchor: A01
Riders obey every traffic law, sign, and signal, halting at each stop sign and red light [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F04 | anchor: A01
Riders always travel with the flow of traffic and never ride against it [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F05 | anchor: A01
A rider sits only on or astride a permanent regular seat and never carries more people than the bicycle was designed or equipped to hold [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F06 | anchor: A01
On a one-way road with at least two marked lanes, a rider keeps as close as possible to the left curb or edge [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F07 | anchor: A01
Two riders side by side on a laned road share one lane and must not block the movement of traffic [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F08 | anchor: A01
Riders are allowed to use the shoulder of the road [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F09 | anchor: A01
Riders signal with their arms: a right turn means the left arm up or the right arm held flat, a left turn means the left arm held flat, and a stop means the left arm pointed down [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F10 | anchor: A01
A rider moving slower than surrounding traffic stays as close as possible to the right curb or edge, except when passing another vehicle, preparing a left turn, avoiding hazards such as parked cars or debris, or riding an outside lane narrower than 14 feet or too tight for a bicycle and car to travel side by side [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F11 | anchor: A01
A rider never hitches the bicycle or their body to a moving streetcar or vehicle on the road [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F12 | anchor: A01
A rider never carries a package, bundle, or object that stops them from keeping at least one hand on the handlebars [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F13 | anchor: A01
Shared lane markings help riders position themselves away from opening car doors and in lanes too narrow to share, show road users where riders are likely to be, promote safe passing, and discourage wrong-way riding [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0068]

FACT_ID: sec13-F14 | anchor: A02
Each bicycle needs a brake strong enough to skid its wheels on dry, level, clean pavement [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F15 | anchor: A02
Riders with hearing loss may show a safety flag on the bicycle [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F16 | anchor: A02
At night a bicycle carries a front white lamp seen from at least 500 feet ahead plus a red DPS-approved rear reflector seen from 50 to 300 feet, with an optional red rear light seen from 500 feet allowed alongside the reflector [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F17 | anchor: A02
Local laws may require a rider to wear a helmet [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F18 | anchor: A02
Riders slow down and stay careful on walkways shared with pedestrians, never weave between parked cars, and pull fully off the street to stop, park, or fix the bicycle [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F19 | anchor: A02
Riders pick routes that fit their skill and experience, may fit a mirror, and wear light or reflective clothing so drivers can spot them [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0069]

FACT_ID: sec13-F20 | anchor: A02
In rain, riders watch for slick manholes and painted stripes, hidden water-filled potholes, and drivers whose visibility drops sharply [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-tx-c:texas-department-of-public-safety-driver:handbook:pdf-0069]
